People of Voat, if you proposed marriage, what prompted you to do so?

• I wanted to get married. So I made a proposal.
  • We lived in separate states at the time. I waited until I was visiting to do it.
  • Not really. I proposed about a year after we met and 5 months after we became a couple.
  • Planned. I worked something out with a planetarium for a private showing. It had a private significance for us. When the lights came up, I proposed.

I was very opposed to marriage for a long time. But there came a point where I decided that my SO's desire to get married was stronger than my desire not to. I wanted to make him happy by marrying him, since it was so important to him. So, I proposed. It took me three years after the proposal to be ready for the actual wedding to take place, but we finally got married this past May. I still don't feel like it's something I had to do in life to make me feel complete or whatever, but it made me happy to make him so happy. So, it was worth it.

I thought my husband was about to propose to me one night at dinner - started the whole, "I love you very much" spiel - but I didn't want to get married (in general, not just to him), so I spouted out the first thing I could think of to cut him off and shut him up. Unfortunately, the first thing I thought of "Let's get married!" He just glared at me and said (very vindictively, I might add), "Yes." He wouldn't let me take it back so we were engaged all through dinner and by the time we were done I realized I rather liked it, so I "dis-engaged" us in the parking lot so he could do the knee thing, all proper like.

It was definitely spontaneous. We'd been dating for about four or five months, and I had planned on never getting married, collecting a million cats, and dying single and happy, but I guess his way works too!
Well, I liked her and her brother has a brewery.

I didn't propose, but i did "instigate" a proposal.

I wanted to get married for social reasons, basically. I wanted my family and friends to think of me and my relationship differently. Unfortunately now that it's all said and done, getting married was a pretty silly idea. The party was fun and all, we did something low budget that was worth the money we spent, and no one went into debt over it. But honestly I don't like being married at all. I refuse to change my name and thus far we haven't reaped any other benefits (taxes still filed separately, no shared health insurance, etc). It didn't change my relationships with anyone, my husband included. The only thing that changed was that I consistently get mail from older relatives to the wrong name.
